title_note:
⚠️ DELIBERATE VidIQ-FLOOR OVERRIDE (user, 2026-08-02). Lead scores 21-31, under the >=60 new-ship bar. Reason: the >=60 pool in sleep/anxiety/calm_relax is EXHAUSTED — of 10 banked phrases >=60 in these lanes, 8 are past-locks, same-concept, A/B losers or anti-patterns; only 'music before bed' (61) and 'relaxing instrumental music' (70) survive, and the second is textbook generic-soft. The prescreener itself now returns the contradiction: 'peaceful music for sleep' scores 62 AND is rejected as anti-pattern:generic_soft_framing_leads. The floor and the generic-soft anti-pattern disqualify each other, so the floor is not functioning as a gate. Counter-evidence to title rule (1) 'higher VidIQ = better lead' (which rests on n=2 concluded tests): 'Music to Sleep Through the Night' (CTR 7.15, best at scale) and 'Quiet Night Music' (6.53, 35.5% T1) are both distinctive low-search-volume leads. VidIQ measures SEARCH, which is 17% of channel traffic vs 27% suggested and 36% subscriber. THIS WEEK IS THE TEST: 3 ships at 30-31 against Monday's 66. If the low scorers land at or above the recent ~3% CTR floor, rule (1) needs re-derivation on a bigger sample.

⚠️ n=1 CELL. This is a coin flip, not a forecast. Recorded so the outcome is not read as evidence either way without more ships.

B leads with 'Music to Settle Your Mind' (FRESH, preflight 47 chars PASS). A is somatic (breathing), B is cognitive (mind) — two different framings of the same anxiety state, which is a real second hypothesis.

⚠️ HOW TO USE THE B VARIANT — unresolved as of 2026-08-02, written to serve either case. YouTube's Test & Compare varies THUMBNAILS only; there is no native simultaneous title A/B. So B is EITHER (a) a sequential swap — ship A, switch to B after ~7d, compare like-for-like periods — OR (b) a documented fallback if A hits a conflict at upload. If you run (a), log it to ab_raw_data.csv as a title test and note the swap date, because the comparison is across time rather than concurrent and is therefore confounded by decay. If (b), record that B was never live so a future read does not treat it as a tested-and-lost variant.

thumbnail_text_variants.strategy:
Verb + comparative, mirroring 'SLEEP BETTER' (6.83 / 6.71). 14 chars, mid mobile band. Dedup 0 hits across all briefs and the thumbnail dataset. Pairs with the title as promise-and-method: the thumb says what you get, the title says how.

⚠️ CHOSEN ON FIT, NOT ON FORMAT — and an earlier version of this note claimed otherwise. Correcting it here:

The anxiety lane shows NO measurable format preference. Cross-tabbing lane × format_class × CTR: outcome-imperative 3.50 (n=5) vs Q-hook 3.52 (n=8). Indistinguishable. Same in sleep (5.39 vs 5.33) and morning (4.10 vs 4.20).

The channel-wide pattern that looked like 'imperatives beat Q-hooks 14:4' is a LANE-MIX ARTIFACT — imperatives cluster in sleep and morning, which are simply the highest-CTR lanes. Split by lane and it dissolves. Simpson's paradox.

The ONE lane with a real format effect is COGNITIVE: Q-hook 3.52 (n=7) vs imperative 2.87 (n=8). The banked thumbnail_format_rules 3/3 for Q-hooks holds there and should be kept. It is NOT supported in anxiety.

For the record, the best-performing anxiety thumbnail on the channel is 'ANXIOUS MIND?' at 4.36 — a Q-hook. 'CHEST TIGHT?' (the original pick) was in that register. Either choice is defensible; this is a coin flip and should not be read as evidence for a format rule in either direction.

⚠️ thumbnail_dataset.csv has no impressions column, so none of these figures are survivor-bias-stripped.

A tanpura may rest at frame edge; it must not be the subject. Overlay 'BREATHE EASIER' in large dark-teal serif with a second tier reading 'Tanpura · Raga Bhimpalasi' — put the text in its own banner panel at ~35% of frame, which is what both competitor breakouts do and what keeps text legible at 120px.
description:
Steady Your Breathing | Slow Tanpura | 1.5 Hours of Give your breath something slow and steady to follow

Your breathing has gone shallow and high in your chest, and you probably have not noticed until now.

This peaceful Indian ambient meditation music is designed to give your breath something slow and steady to follow.

Enjoy 1.5 hours of deep tanpura drone, resonant and unhurried, looped seamlessly so nothing interrupts you.

Perfect for anxious evenings, before a difficult conversation, after bad news, breathwork, panic settling, lying down, meditation, when your mind will not slow, before sleep, whenever your chest feels tight.

🎵 ABOUT THIS MUSIC
Instrument: Tanpura
Raga: Bhimpalasi
Style: Indian classical ambient, instrumental only
Mood: Calm, steady, unhurried
Duration: 1.5 hours

🎧 HOW TO USE
Keep the volume low enough that it sits underneath the room rather than filling it. Headphones deepen the drone, but this works just as well through a speaker.

⏱ CHAPTERS
0:00 — First settling
9:00 — Breath finding its floor
18:00 — Slower
27:00 — Steady
36:00 — Loosening
45:00 — Deeper resonance
54:00 — Quiet holding
63:00 — Even slower
72:00 — Nothing to brace against
81:00 — Coming to rest

⏱ BEST FOR
Anxious evenings
Before a difficult conversation
After bad news
Breathwork practice
Settling a racing heart
Lying down in the dark
Meditation
When your mind will not slow
Before sleep
Whenever your chest feels tight

If this music helped, subscribe to Raga Focus for more uninterrupted Indian ambient healing music.

#SteadyYourBreathing #TanpuraMusic #AnxietyRelief #IndianAmbientMusic
